input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT and a clear failure of the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up mechanic; a take-or-pay shortfall is a penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment) and § 9.4 (Customer's convenience-termination right, under which Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective date). We therefore replace the commitment with the preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with payment only for usage or ordered Services, which is consistent with § 7.1's Order Form fee mechanic.

mappings.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.

proposal.summary: Delete the three-year take-or-pay and confirm no minimum commitment; Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced the USD 2,000,000 annual commitment with our preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with Customer paying only for usage or ordered Services. This also removes the conflict with Sections 9.4 and 12.3; if a commitment is essential, our fallback is one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
